items.title: Mike Vax interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2022
items.q: like on the Kenton band... Von Ohlen’s, 'Boy you’ve got to get that note out because that cymbal is going to try to just eliminate you.'

ctx.x: Sometimes I get the feeling that the surrounding sonority helps that note come out. I don’t know if it’s my imagination. It’s like if I try to play a high note above the range on the saxophone and I tried it in the practice room I’m not going to get it but tonight when the band is playing around you I have a better chance that it might come out.

I think that that helps. Yeah. I think, and part of the challenge of getting to where you can play that, especially for a lead trumpet player, is to be able to do it by yourself with no help. And then when you get with the band I agree with you, all that sonority and everything actually helps. But one of the things that, like on the Kenton band you know what they used to call that huge cymbal, the eliminator, that huge cymbal that Stan had for the band. You know why it was called the eliminator? It eliminated a…

That reminds me of a Joe Wilder story when I think he was on the Hampton band or something. They had this mythical thing called the barracuda that would get rid of things that they didn’t like. I can just see someone losing that cymbal.
